# source of truth: compiler/codegen/src/metal/ (the C++ oracle this was dumped from is deleted)

# @runtime: bytes=39611 fnv1a64=0x310a2f7d72f22fd5

# cases: 192
# re-blessed: the C++ oracle (driver/metal/src/pipeline/m1_codegen.cpp) is
#   deleted, so these bytes can no longer be re-derived from it. Three cases
#   below were re-blessed from Rust in the change that made the emitted corpus
#   compile: `driver/metal/tests/msl_compile_test.cpp` put every kernel here
#   through Apple's shader compiler for the first time and found two rejections
#   the byte comparison could never see, because the oracle had them too.
#     * readiness/commit `wide_30` emitted `[[buffer(31)]]`, one past Metal's
#       highest buffer index; `METAL_M1_MAX_CHANNELS` now rejects it by name.
#     * three grouped fused regions passed the `const device bfloat*` logits
#       pointer into `ptir_m1_execute`'s `const device uchar*` parameter, which
#       MSL will not convert. They now cast.
#   Nothing else in this directory moved, and `msl_compile_test` is the standing
#   check that took over from the oracle for the question it could not answer.
#   re-blessed again (emitter 27): `m1_reduce_argmax` no longer materializes one
#   16-byte candidate per element into device `temporary` and tree-reduces it in
#   passes -- `m1_argmax_combine` is a strict total order, so a fold gives the
#   same answer -- and the bf16 logits intrinsic copies unrolled. Both loops run
#   on the single thread that owns a lane, so at a 248320 vocab they were ~250ms
#   per decode step against a ~4ms model forward. Only @runtime bytes moved.
#   re-blessed again (emitter 29): a generated region now gets a threadgroup per
#   lane instead of a thread, and the three things that walked a vocabulary-wide
#   row -- the logits gather, argmax, and the typed copy behind a reshape -- are
#   split across it. m1_copy_typed also moved from one device access per BYTE to
#   one per word. Between them a decode step's GPU time went 89ms -> 6.5ms.
#   re-blessed again (emitter 31): a same-footprint reshape is a view, so the
#   grouped emitter elides its copy and points the consumers at the source
#   value's offset. The runtime executed it as a byte-for-byte copy of the whole
#   value, which in the sampler's graph was a vocabulary-wide round trip through
#   device memory for nothing.
# REGENERATED: the body below is this compiler's output, not the recorded output of the source of truth above
#   reason: cumsum/cumprod widened from F32-only to every numeric dtype; the m1 runtime's scan block now branches on the operand dtype instead of loading every lane through m1_load_f. The oracle dumps change only because that block is embedded verbatim in every emitted source -- no emitted structure moved, and the f32 path is byte-for-byte the arithmetic the oracle recorded.
